subject: Error: Failed to create the shared library. Is it the Rtools version?

messages.author: 8df77a1c1b1da14e
messages.subject: Error: Failed to create the shared library. Is it the Rtools version?
parts:
I just got a new laptop, and when I tried to compile a model, I got an error Failed to create shared library: 

> Cnim <- compileNimble(nim,showCompilerOutput=TRUE)
compiling... this may take a minute. On some systems there may be some compiler warnings that can be safely ignored.
Warning message:
In system(cmd) : 'make' not found
Error: Failed to create the shared library.


I then realized that my IT tech had not installed Rtools, so I installed Rtools35. The problem persisted (even after a reboot), so I thought maybe I needed Rtools34 instead. I installed it (but it failed to update the Windows registry - not sure if that is a problem), but still no luck compiling. 
Running the following code suggest that R 3.5.0 (the latest version I am authorized to install) needs Rtools35.

> pkgbuild::find_rtools(debug = TRUE)
Scanning R CMD config CC...
cc_path:  
'.exe' does not exist
Scanning path...
Scanning registry...
Found C:/Rtools for 3.4 
Found C:/Rtools for 3.5 
VERSION.txt
Rtools version 3.4.0.1964 
WARNING: Rtools is required to build R packages, but no version of Rtools compatible with R 3.5.0 was found. Rtools 3.5 was previously installed in C:/Rtools but now that directory contains Rtools 3.4.

Please download and install Rtools 3.5 from http://cran.r-project.org/bin/windows/Rtools/.


Is this likely to be Rtools problem, and if so, does it really matter whether I have 34 or 35? The old laptop (which is gone now) definitely also had R 3.5.0, and I am almost certain it had Rtools 34, not 35, so I am puzzled by the message that 34 is not compatible with R 3.5.0.


Thanks,
Glenn

messages.subject: Re: Error: Failed to create the shared library. Is it the Rtools version?
parts:
Hi Glenn,

It's hard for us to diagnose what seem to be system-specific issues.

On Windows, when installing Rtools, it is important to be sure to check the box that tells it to modify the PATH system variable.

If that doesn't help, I suggest as a first step to try to diagnose Rtools installation issues outside of nimble, such as with a simple Rcpp example (easy to find online).

-Perry

messages.author: 8df77a1c1b1da14e
messages.subject: Re: Error: Failed to create the shared library. Is it the Rtools version?
parts:
Perry,
Thanks for the reply - I was out a few days and didn't see it until this morning.

I tried a few things and have not resolved the problem. 

1) I had failed to properly uninstall Rtools 3.5 before I tried to install Rtools 3.4, so that may have been the problem with the note about "Rtools 3.5 was previously installed..." Uninstalling, and then reinstalling made that message go away, and it seems that find_rtools(debug=TRUE) successfully find Rtools regardless of whether I installed Rtools 3.5 or 3.4. But the nimble model won't compile either way.

2) I tried a few of the examples in the package RcppExamples, and they all seemed to work. So, if Rtools is required for those to work, then it seems that things are working on that front.

3) Rtools 3.5 installs without errors, but it appears that there is not an option to modify the PATH system variable, as there is with Rtools 3.4. Not sure what that means for nimble.

4) When I install Rtools 3.4 (checking the box to modify PATH), I encounter an error: 

Error creating registry key:
HKEY_LOCAL_MACHINE\SYSTEM\CurrentControlSet\Control\Session Manager\Environment

RegCreateKeyEx Failed; code S.
Access is denied.

Click Retry to try again, Ignore to proceed anyway, or Abort to cancel installation.

5) Clicking Ignore to proceed anyway does seem to go ahead and install Rtools anyway, and find_rtools(debug=TRUE) does find it, and the examples from RcppExamples do seem to work. But my nimble model still won't compile.

6) when I install Rtools 3.4 (checking the box for PATH, but unchecking the box to modify the registry key), I still get the same error message, and find_rtools() still returns TRUE, and the examples from RcppExamples still succeed. However, find_rtools(debug==TRUE) returns the following:

Scanning R CMD config CC...
cc_path:  
'.exe' does not exist
Scanning path...
Scanning registry...
WARNING: Rtools is required to build R packages, but is not currently installed.
Please download and install Rtools 3.5 from http://cran.r-project.org/bin/windows/Rtools/.

So, I suspect the you are right and that it is a system-specific issue. I think my best guess (but it is just a guess), is that maybe nimble really does not work with Rtool 3.5 (no option to modify PATH), and the missing registry key for Rtools 3.4 (maybe because I installed Rtools 3.5 first) is also now preventing proper function of 3.4. I will see if I can take this up with my IT guy and resolve the registry issue. But if others have had success with Rtools 3.5 (this is now the recommended version on the install page), then clearly that is not my problem.

Thanks again for the suggestions.
Glenn

messages.author: dd632bd3bbcdd7e9
messages.subject: Re: Error: Failed to create the shared library. Is it the Rtools version?
parts:
Hi Glenn,

I was able to install everything on Windows from the ground up: R 3.6.0, Rtools 3.5, then nimble, with no problems.  I see you are required to work on R 3.5.0.  I did not attempt to go back to that and check everything.

You noted Rtools 3.5 did not ask you about the PATH variable.  When I installed it, it showed a checkbox for “Add rtools to system PATH”, which I needed to check.

If you need to work locally (i.e. not in directories requiring admin privileges), I think it is possible.  You can install packages locally by options in install.packages() and library().  One way to automate that is to use .libPaths("directory_you_want") in a .Rprofile file.  I believe you do need to be careful when upgrading R, as the locally-installed packages may then fall out of date.  I think it is also possible to install Rtools locally, although I've never tried it.

I hope it helps.  If you figure out a solution on your system that might be useful to others, please share it.

-Perry

Thanks Carl and Perry,

I think I am up and running now. I didn't know about a '.Renviron' file, but I defined a '.Rprofile' file, located in the  Sys.getenv("HOME") directory and put this line in it: 
Sys.setenv(PATH = paste("C:/Rtools/bin", Sys.getenv("PATH"), sep=";"))

and now things seem to work as they should.
